steps.title: Useful words & phrases
steps.intro: Key words for this chapter — all appear in the dialogues.

steps.title: La hotel
steps.context: Mike Foster, a businessman from Scotland, has just arrived in Bucharest. He sees an empty seat next to a young woman in the hotel lobby.

lines.speaker: Mike
lines.ro: Bună dimineața, domnișoară. E liber aici, vă rog?
lines.en: Good morning, miss. Is this seat free, please?

lines.speaker: Domnișoară
lines.en: Yes. Please, go ahead and sit down.

lines.speaker: Mike
lines.en: Thank you. Are you staying in the hotel?

lines.speaker: Domnișoară
lines.en: Yes, I am staying right here.

lines.speaker: Mike
lines.en: Are you from Romania?

lines.speaker: Domnișoară
lines.ro: Da, sunt româncă. Sunt din Timișoara. Dar dumneavoastră?
lines.en: Yes, I am Romanian. I am from Timișoara. And you?

lines.speaker: Mike
lines.ro: Eu sunt din Marea Britanie, din Edinburgh. Sunt scoțian. Și cât timp stați în București?
lines.en: I am from Britain, from Edinburgh. I am Scottish. And how long are you staying in Bucharest?

lines.speaker: Domnișoară
lines.ro: Stau numai patru zile. Dar dumneavoastră?
lines.en: I am only staying four days. And you?

lines.speaker: Mike
lines.ro: Eu stau trei luni. Sunt om de afaceri. Mă numesc Mike Foster. Și dvs?
lines.en: I am staying three months. I am a businessman. My name is Mike Foster. And yours?

lines.speaker: Domnișoară
lines.ro: Eu sunt Rodica Mihai, sunt ziaristă la ziarul 'Azi'.
lines.en: I am Rodica Mihai. I am a journalist at the newspaper 'Today'.

lines.speaker: Mike
lines.en: Is what you do interesting?

lines.speaker: Domnișoară
lines.ro: În general, da. Vorbiți limba română?
lines.en: In general, yes. Do you speak Romanian?

lines.speaker: Mike
lines.en: Unfortunately, not very well.

steps.title: Introducing yourself
steps.explanation: When asking a stranger for help, use vă rog with the appropriate form of address. Notice how Mike used this in the dialogue, and how poftiți was the natural reply.
steps.callout: In Dialogue 1, Mike said vă rog, domnișoară to ask for the seat. The young lady replied with poftiți — these two form a natural request-permission pair.

steps.title: Nationality
steps.explanation: In Romanian, nationality words change form to agree with the gender of the person. Notice the different endings for masculine and feminine.
steps.callout: Unlike English, nationalities in Romanian are written with a small letter. Only country names get a capital: Anglia, România, Franța.

steps.title: Pronouns & forms of 'you'
steps.explanation: Romanian has four forms of 'you'. The persons of the verb are listed below.
steps.callout: Mike and Rodica use dumneavoastră throughout — the polite form. Tu would be used only with a close friend or family member.

steps.title: The verbs a fi, a sta, a face, a locui
steps.intro: These four verbs appeared in the dialogue. Here are their full present tense conjugations.

tables.meaning: to stay, to stand, to reside

steps.title: În lift
steps.context: Mike and Rodica meet again in the hotel lift. Rodica asks Mike how to spell his surname.

lines.speaker: Rodica
lines.en: Good evening, what a coincidence!

lines.speaker: Mike
lines.en: Indeed. What floor do you want?

lines.speaker: Rodica
lines.en: The twelfth. And you?

lines.speaker: Mike
lines.en: The ninth.

lines.speaker: Rodica
lines.ro: Scuzați-mă, dar cum se scrie numele dumneavoastră de familie?
lines.en: Excuse me, but how do you spell your surname?

lines.speaker: Mike
lines.ro: Foster. F - o - s - t - e - r.
lines.en: Foster. F - o - s - t - e - r.

lines.speaker: Rodica
lines.en: Thank you. Here is the ninth floor.

lines.speaker: Mike
lines.en: Thank you, goodbye.

lines.speaker: Rodica
lines.en: See you soon, Mike Foster.

steps.title: Greetings
steps.explanation: In Dialogue 2 we met Bună seara. Here is the full set of Romanian greetings, from formal to informal.

steps.title: Numbers 0–100
steps.explanation: Romanian numbers follow a regular pattern. From 20 upward, de is added before a noun. In informal speech, -sprezece is clipped to -șpe.

examples.ro: zero, unu, doi, trei, patru, cinci
douăzeci de ani (not cincisprezece de ani)

steps.callout: Colloquial clipping: unsprezece → unșpe, doisprezece → doișpe, etc. You will hear this constantly in everyday speech.

steps.title: Negation
steps.explanation: To make a negative statement, place nu directly before the verb. Romanian also uses double negatives — this is correct grammar, not a mistake.

examples.en: No, I don't live in Washington.
I have nothing. (lit. I don't have nothing)
I never stay at a hotel.

steps.callout: Double negatives like Nimeni nu face nimic are grammatically correct in Romanian. This is different from English, where double negatives are considered errors.

items.prompt: How do you spell your name?
